extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers and readers of Nature Communications / academic researchers interested in journal peer-review policy
extracted.subtask_description: Description of Nature Communications' trial and implementation of transparent peer review (publishing reviewer reports and author rebuttals) and the operational/ethical criteria for running that scheme. Covers consent rules, anonymity handling, uptake metrics and observed impacts after one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviewer reports and author rebuttal letters
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish reviewer reports and author rebuttal letters for papers submitted from January 2016 onwards, but only if authors agree to this upon acceptance of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intention is to open up the peer review process at the journal, and to provide information on the expert reports that led to the editorial decision to publish a paper. The peer review files can serve as background on the merits of a study and inform about the discussion between authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-in consent upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to agree to publication of the peer review files upon acceptance of the paper; authors do have the option to opt out of the scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opt-in rate is treated as crucial to the success of transparent peer review; average opt-in across the journal after one year was about 60%. Uptake varies by research area (higher where open peer review is more commonplace). Despite opt-out being available, in almost all research areas the majority of published papers will now contain a peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer agreement to potential publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must agree to the potential publication of their reviewer reports (i.e., reviewers cannot opt out of the policy when asked to review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement has only been a problem for a small number of reviewers, who declined to review under this circumstance. Some objections stem from concerns that in small research areas it may be easy to deduce a reviewer's identity from published reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of reviewer anonymity unless signed
rubrics_metrics.description: The anonymity of our reviewers is maintained, unless they sign their reports to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity is preserved by default to protect reviewers, but reviewers may choose to sign reports. The journal recognises a residual risk that identities could be deduced in niche fields, which has led to occasional reviewer refusal to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use opt-in rate by research area as success metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The rate at which authors are opting in to publish peer review files is used as a key metric to judge the success of transparent peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data were collected for 787 qualifying papers and displayed by research area; average opt-in ~60%. Variation by field is expected and informs evaluation of the scheme's acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timing of policy (qualifying papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent peer review applies to papers submitted from January 2016 onwards (the trial period) and to qualifying papers indexed in the journal's dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial reports on 787 qualifying papers indexed by research area to assess uptake and effects during the first year of the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review files should provide background and inform readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Published reviewer reports and rebuttal letters are intended to give readers information on the expert reports that led to publication and to provide background on the merits of a study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review files can help readers appreciate the value of published papers, and can initiate constructive dialogue between authors and readers about specifics of a study. Authors have, in some instances, promoted positive published reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reader engagement and qualitative feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader feedback and usage statistics (e.g., number of downloads of peer review files) are relevant measures of the policy's impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although feedback was limited in the first year, the journal suggests studying download numbers and reports anecdotal instances of readers engaging with peer review discussions and authors promoting reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy permanence decision based on trial outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will decide on making transparent peer review a permanent feature based on the trial's uptake and observed benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After one year and an average ~60% author opt-in, Nature Communications concluded it was encouraged by the response and elected to make transparent peer review a permanent feature, with the expectation that appreciation of benefits will grow over time.
